binders: q is an arbitrary function from Real × Real to Real, written q(x,t).
speed is an arbitrary real number.
x is an arbitrary real spatial evaluation point.
t is an arbitrary real temporal evaluation point.
conclusions: The one-component matrix/vector formulation at (x,t) is logically equivalent to the scalar formulation at (x,t).

Explicitly, there exist qt,qx : Fin 1 → Real such that τ ↦ (i ↦ q(x,τ)) has derivative qt at t, ξ ↦ (i ↦ q(ξ,t)) has derivative qx at x, and qt + A qx = 0, if and only if there exist a,b ∈ Real such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative a at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative b at x, and a + speed·b = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Fin 1 is a singleton index set.
The vectorized field is q̃(x,t)(i) = q(x,t) for the unique i ∈ Fin 1.
The coefficient matrix A is the 1-by-1 matrix A(i,j) = speed.
For the unique component, (A qx)(i) = speed·qx(i).
HasDerivAt for τ ↦ q(x,τ) and ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) expresses the time and space partial derivatives at the fixed point, respectively.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real-valued function q of two real variables, every real speed, and every point (x,t), encoding q as a one-component vector and speed as a 1-by-1 matrix does not change the pointwise transport condition: the vector field has time and space derivatives whose residual qt + [speed] qx is the zero vector exactly when q has scalar time and space derivatives whose residual is qt + speed·qx = 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is pointwise at one arbitrary (x,t); it does not assert differentiability or the transport equation on a neighborhood or globally.
There is no differentiability hypothesis on q. Each side itself requires the relevant two derivatives to exist through existential derivative witnesses.

Because the conclusion is an equivalence rather than an assertion that either transport condition holds, it remains true when both sides are false, for example when a required partial derivative does not exist.
The spatial and temporal domains are all of Real; no boundary, interval, initial-value, or regularity conditions are encoded.
The parameter speed is an unrestricted constant real number and may be zero or negative; it is not a function of x or t.
The matrix/vector formulation has exactly one component. It does not establish a genuinely higher-dimensional system result.

The two derivative witnesses on each side are constrained both to be the corresponding derivatives and to satisfy the residual equation; no independent values or extra relationship between x and t are imposed.
No claim about existence, uniqueness, propagation, conservation, or solutions of a PDE beyond this pointwise representational equivalence is encoded.
